findings.title: The new site list names the wrong `baselines/review.txt` entry, and only ONE of the two sites evades the obvious grep
findings.summary: The clause reads: 'TWO COMMITTED SITES CARRY THE LOAD-MEASURED FIGURE and both evade the obvious grep: `LocalSequencerRenewTest`'s slack comment, which wraps `load` and `average` across two lines ... and the `rounds:M4.17` entry in `baselines/review.txt`.' Half of it verifies and half does not. VERIFIED: `grep -c 'load average' sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/LocalSequencerRenewTest.java` returns 0 -- the comment at :389-390 breaks as 'even at load' / 'average 124' -- and it does say 124 where the twelve verdict occurrences all say 123 (the single 'average 124' under `.harness/review/` is a test-reviewer QUOTING that comment). NOT VERIFIED: the entry carrying the load-measured figure is `rounds:M4.43`, not `rounds:M4.17`. `rounds:M4.43` reads 'THE TEST REVIEWER measured the 2x mutant killed in 3 of 7 runs ... honest never below 6 including at load average 123. THE PRODUCTION REVIEWER re-measured independently, recording `fast=6, 7, 7` for the 2x mutant at a 2000ms window' -- both contaminated series, named per role. `rounds:M4.17` contains no load figure at all: its nearest sentence is '`multipliedBy(2)` landed exactly on an inclusive floor of 3 and survived. The floor is 4 now', which M4.41's own row (backlog-notes.md:309) already diagnoses separately and differently -- 'literally TRUE of the code ... what is unsupported is what it carries in context'. And that occurrence does NOT evade the obvious grep: `grep -rn 'load average' baselines/review.txt` returns it, one hit, in plain text. Related undercount in the same clause: 'TWO COMMITTED SITES' misses M4.41's own notes row, which carries 'honest never dropped below 6 across seven runs including load average 123'.
findings.failure_scenario: This clause is the correction checklist -- it is the only place in the tree that says WHERE the contaminated figures are committed. A session working the row opens `baselines/review.txt`, greps `rounds:M4.17` as instructed, reads 'The floor is 4 now', finds it literally true of `isBetween(4L, 30L)`, concludes there is nothing to correct in that file, and leaves the actually-contaminated sentence standing three entries down in `rounds:M4.43`. That is verbatim the correct-one-copy-miss-the-duplicate failure the SIBLING ROW IN THIS SAME COMMIT (M4.45) is filed about and which commit 17e54d6 records twice, reproduced inside the row that lists the copies. The second-order cost is the same as round 1's: a session that checks the pointer finds `rounds:M4.17` carries no load figure at all and cannot tell whether the row means a different entry or invented the citation. Fix, if taken, is two tokens -- `rounds:M4.43` -- plus dropping 'both' from 'both evade the obvious grep', since only the Java comment does.

findings.title: The refuted 'sleeps overrun, so the floor is conservative' reasoning is not only in an earlier draft -- it is committed in HEAD's own body, and the row does not name it
findings.summary: The new clause says 'THE DIRECTION IS NOT SAFE, and an earlier draft of this row claimed it was on the ground that `Thread.sleep` overruns rather than undershoots so an honest rate under load is a floor. THAT REASONING IS WRONG HERE'. The technical correction checks out: the measurement window IS a `Thread.sleep` -- LocalSequencerRenewTest.java:415 `Thread.sleep(1000)` against a 150ms interval (:138) and `isBetween(4L, 30L)` (:422) -- so an overrun raises the count through the window and lowers it through the renewer's sleeps, 1000/300 = 3.33 can reach 4, and the recorded series 6 idle / 6 under 32 spinners / 7 at load 123 does have the loaded sample highest, with the committed 1.75x being 7/4 and the idle sample giving 1.5. What the clause gets wrong is WHERE the refuted reasoning lives. It is not confined to an unlanded draft: commit 17e54d6 (HEAD, `M4.8: split checkpoints into M4.8a-c before building any of it`) carries it in its body, in the ENVIRONMENTAL paragraph that first records this leak -- 'Sleeps overrun rather than undershoot, so honest-rate floors measured under it are conservative -- but the robustness claims meant less than they appeared.' Same reasoning, near-identical wording, permanent and uneditable.
findings.failure_scenario: 17e54d6's body is currently the ONLY landed record of the leak -- the M0.75 row is still `todo` -- so it is what `git log --grep` archaeology reaches first when someone asks why the M4.41 numbers are suspect. That session reads 'honest-rate floors measured under it are conservative', concludes the direction is safe and no re-measurement is owed, and never re-opens the mutant-survival question that this row now says is OPEN. A session that reads both cannot tell which is current, because nothing cross-references them. A commit message cannot be edited, so the remedy is additive and one clause: name 17e54d6's body as the standing copy, exactly as M4.42 and M4.45 name their duplicates. Leaving it is the shape M4.45 -- filed in this same diff -- exists to punish.

A floor of 9 clears both modes'). (5) MINOR R-M4.45-1(b) fixed: both rows carry '; round-2 review measured exactly that', matching FakeSequencerTest.java:207-210 character for character. Swept every remaining citation in the two rows: M4.1's landed record (backlog-done.md:110, 'at three streams a broken sort still produced the asserted order about 1 run in 6') ✓; 1-in-720 = 1/6! and the six-key fixture ✓; 'M4.8a's prescription now says the opposite in its own words' (backlog-notes.md:319, 'STATED THE RIGHT WAY ROUND') ✓; 'the M4.8 split commit records twice' ✓ (17e54d6 body: the four-false-claims paragraph, 'fixed in one clause and left standing in its duplicate three clauses later', and recorded minor 6, whose 'found by a reviewer grepping `*.java` where mine covered only docs' the row quotes). Two citations in the NEW prose do not hold, both minor and both filed. Still unverifiable and stated as such last round: the process counts, `RN` state, `/init` reparenting, two-hour lifetime and the batched-vs-individual `kill -9` behaviour are this session's own observations with no artifact behind them, though 202 and load 206 agree with 17e54d6's body. Docs only: no object-store request is added or changed, nothing is stated in the present tense that does not exist (both rows are `todo` and prescribe no mechanism), and the M4.45 summary still drops 'At three keys' as round 1 recorded -- unchanged, still minor, and not worth another round. ⚠️ ONE HARNESS FACT THE PARENT MUST ACT ON: `.harness/review/8ced8150....test-reviewer.json` recorded the PREVIOUS hash under `"task": "M0.65"` while its finding ids read TR-M0.75-*; if the test-reviewer records these bytes under M0.65 again while this verdict names M0.75, `review_rounds.py` raises 'verdicts for <sha> disagree about the task' and `check-reviewed.sh` fails closed.
